title: BEADS: Bias Evaluation Across Domains
benchmark_measurement: The benchmark measured bias against religious groups through several tasks: 1) Bias Rate, which quantifies the tendency of models to associate religious identity mentions (Christian, Jewish, Muslim) with biased content in token prediction tasks. 2) Demographic Variation, which assesses if models misclassify neutral statements as biased when religious identifiers (Christian, Muslim, Hindu, Buddhist) are included. 3) Stereotype Alignment, which evaluates how models agree or disagree with stereotypes about various religious groups.
findings: Smaller models like BERT and RoBERTa exacerbated biases for religious groups in token prediction tasks, with RoBERTa showing the highest bias rates for Christian (51.1%) and Jewish (59.6%) identities. Llama2-7B-chat and Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2 were prone to misclassifying neutral sentences as biased for Muslim and Christian groups. When presented with stereotypes, the Llama2 model showed higher agreement with stereotypes about Muslims and Christians compared to the Mistral model, which showed low agreement.
